newsitem.title: NORWAY: Bank shares heavily traded on Oslo Bourse.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares heavily traded on Oslo Bourse.

text.p: Trade in bank shares dominated the Norwegian stock exchange on Wednesday with Fokus Bank and Den norske Bank (DnB) accounting for more than half of the volume.

Oslo's Total index closed 0.23 percent lower at 1,071.13 points in staggering turnover of 2.2 million crowns. Fokus, which is battling a hostile takeover bid, was the most traded stock for the third consecutive day at 832 million crowns.
The share closed unchanged at 73 crowns, the price offered to Fokus shareholders on Monday by Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 regional savings banks seeking to carve up Fokus.
Analysts speculated a foreign bank may make a rival bid for Fokus, rescuing it from being taken over by Sparebankgruppen.
DnB, which is fighting a separate battle against Fokus for mortgage lender BNbank, was traded for 557 million crowns. The share ended marginally higher at 21.10 crowns.
DnB on Wednesday raised its cash offer for BNbank to 209 crowns per share from 207 crowns, including dividend. BNbank closed 3.50 crowns higher at 210.
Industrial conglomerate Norsk Hydro was the third most traded share at 210 million crowns, closing unchanged.
